newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - June 13.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - June 13.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Discounting by sawmills drew in buyers early in the week, putting prices on a firmer footing by Thursday, Random Lengths said in its end-week cash lumber update. Prices recouped most of their earlier losses in late-week trading but some failed to come all the way back, the reporting agency said.

The South was particularly active in the latter half of the week, despite persistent wet weather. Supply uncertainty played a part in the firmer tone, although buyers remained skeptical about producer efforts to talk the market higher.

Scattered seasonal sawmill closures in late June and early July relieved selling pressure on some producers in both the U.S. and Canada. Labor talks in British Columbia remained on traders' minds, though the lack of hard news about the subject kept it on the back burner. Weary of the topic, buyers tended to dismiss talk that quota problems would keep some Canadian wood north of the border until after July 1, the agency said.
In the final analysis, most buyers remained convinced that supplies will remain ample, barring an extended strike in Western Canada, Random Lengths said.

Wholesalers got the ball rolling wqhen they covered short positions in response to discounting by mills. Distributors bought a fair volume of replacement wood but remained cautious about booking too far ahead. Secondaries of all types reported stiff competition for sales, which crimped margins, extended turn rates, and kept volumes below year-ago levels. Trucks were in short supply across most of the South as produce season added to problems brought on by lack of qualified drivers, it said.
Railcar supplies were also tight in both the South and the West, it said.
Boards traded steadily, keeping prices firm to higher, but prices of Ponderosa iondustrials were flat to soft.
